speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific symptoms like grunting, nasal flaring, or chest retractions? Also, what was the mode of your delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the preterm birth and maternal gestational diabetes, have you observed cyanosis, especially around the lips, or a "grunting" sound when the baby breathes? Additionally, have the caregivers tried to suction the nose or mouth since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Blood_Gas_Analysis; REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay. Based on these findings, do you have any family history of genetic lung diseases or recent aspiration events?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
